skill.name: Linking words between ideas (however, as a result, meanwhile)
skill.why: Linking words tell readers how two ideas connect, so the meaning is clear.
skill.how: Ask how the ideas connect: a contrast, a result, the same time, or one more.

steps.say: I practised my joke all week. Then: total silence.
show: Mo practised his joke all week. ___ nobody laughed.
steps.ask: Which linking word fits the gap?

options.reason: Did practising cause the silence? Practice should get laughs!
Silence isn't one more good thing. It goes against what you'd expect.

steps.win: Yes! 'However' shows a surprise or opposite. That's a contrast.

steps.say: Linking words, or connectives, show how ideas connect.

show.nudge: That adds one more thing. Which word shows the spill caused something?
That shows the same time. Which word shows the spill caused something?

steps.ask: Tap the linking word that shows a result.
steps.win: The spill caused the glow. 'As a result' shows that.

steps.say: Two things can happen at once, in two places.
show: Zed was gaming in the hut. ___ down at the beach, Wren was building a sandcastle.
steps.ask: Which linking word fits the gap?

options.reason: Did gaming make Wren build a sandcastle? Look at the two places.
Is there a surprise? Two things are just happening at once.

steps.win: Yes! 'Meanwhile' means at the same time, not next.

steps.say: Some people stick 'However' on anything. Check the link first.
show: Zed forgot to charge his tablet. ___ it went flat in the boss fight.
steps.ask: Which linking word fits the gap?

options.reason: Is it a surprise? A flat tablet is just what you'd expect!
These don't happen at once. One thing causes the other.

steps.win: Not charging caused the flat tablet. Check the link first.

steps.say: Nevertheless means however. Consequently means as a result. Furthermore means also.
show: Gus's robot fell off the ladder.

show.nudge: That means 'as a result'. Did falling help it win?
That means 'in addition'. Is winning one more bad thing?

steps.ask: Tap the word that fits before 'it still won the race'.
steps.win: Yes! Expected to lose, but won. 'Nevertheless' shows that contrast.

terms.means: A surprise or the opposite: however, nevertheless, even so, on the other hand.
One thing caused the next: as a result, consequently, for this reason.
Two things at once: meanwhile, at that very moment.
Adds another: in addition, furthermore, on top of that, also.

card.test: Ask how the ideas connect: a surprise, a cause, the same time, or one more?

creature.name: Tethrin
creature.blurb: An orb-weaving spider from the snow gums that spins a silk bridge between two ideas. The bridge only holds if the linking word fits.

write.ask: Join these two ideas with a linking word that shows how they connect.

It threw all the cushions out the window.
checks: I used a linking word, such as However
My linking word shows how the ideas connect
I put a comma after the linking word

encounters.frame: Gus is writing a report called 'Why Snot Is Brilliant'. The Tethrin is keeping well back.
encounters.text: Most people think snot is disgusting, but Gus thinks it is one of the best things about the human body. Your nose makes snot all day, every day, even when you don't have a cold. encounters.text: Living on a space station sounds glamorous, but it comes with some unusual problems. The Bluegum is the size of a small house. Six astronauts live on it for six months at a time. The crew of the station Bluegum sleep in sleeping bags strapped to the wall, so they don't drift into each other in the night. Their food comes in pouches, and they drink through straws, because an open cup of juice would turn into a floating, wobbly ball. On their third day, the station's only toilet broke. encounters.frame: Wren is writing a Field Guide entry on box jellyfish. The Tethrin is very glad it lives on a mountain.
encounters.text: Box jellyfish drift through the warm waters of northern Australia, and they are among the most venomous animals on Earth. Their bodies are almost see-through, shaped like a pale box, and each one trails up to sixty tentacles that can stretch three metres long. Every tentacle is lined with thousands of tiny stinging cells, which fire like microscopic harpoons the moment they touch skin. A single sting can be agonising, and a serious one can be deadly to a human, which is why swimmers in the north wear stinger suits and swim inside netted areas during the summer months. Box jellyfish are not like other jellyfish. They can swim, rather than just drift. They even have eyes, twenty-four of them. Most animals in the sea keep well away from box jellyfish. Fish dart away from them. Crabs hide. ___, some sea turtles eat them without seeming to notice the stings at all, munching through their tentacles like noodles. Scientists are still working out exactly how the turtles do it. Wren thinks the turtles deserve a medal, and possibly a stinger suit of their own.

items.reason: This adds one more problem with the hut.

items.text: The Architect told Mo never to cook on the ladders. ___, Mo fried an egg on rung forty-two.
items.reason: Mo was told not to, and he did it anyway. That goes against what you'd expect.

items.text: Mo's joke book weighs four kilograms. ___, the crew made him leave it at the bottom of the tower.

encounters.frame: Gus is writing a report called 'In Praise of Earwax'. The Tethrin is covering its ears, all eight of them.
encounters.text: Gus is fascinated by earwax, and he wants everyone else to be too. He has written a whole report about it. He has drawn diagrams. He has even brought samples to school, which his teacher asked him to take home. Earwax is made by tiny glands in the skin of your ear canal, and it comes in two main types: a wet, sticky, honey-coloured kind and a dry, flaky, grey kind. Which type you have depends on your family, a bit like the colour of your eyes. Gus says earwax is not dirt at all, but a clever piece of body engineering. It slowly moves outwards from deep inside your ear, carried along by the movement of your jaw every time you talk or chew. Along the way, it traps dust, dirt and the occasional tiny insect before they can reach your eardrum. ___, it contains natural chemicals that help fight off germs, which keeps the inside of your ear healthy. Gus once made candles out of his own earwax, which smelled like old cheese. He does not recommend trying this at home.
encounters.prompt: Gus wants 'Furthermore,' in the gap. Mo wants 'As a result,'. Who is right, and why?
encounters.success: Gus is right. Fighting germs is one more job earwax does, so 'Furthermore' adds it.

options.text: Gus, because fighting germs is one more job, not a result.
Mo, because trapping dirt is what lets earwax fight germs.
options.reason: Nothing says trapping dirt causes it. The germ-fighting chemicals are a separate fact.

options.text: Gus, because the germ-fighting fact is a contrast with the dust fact.
options.reason: Both are helpful jobs earwax does. Nothing is opposite, so it adds one more idea.

options.text: Mo, because the chemicals keep your ear healthy, and that's a result.
options.reason: That result is inside the sentence. The link before it adds one more job.
